claims.text: Integrating machine-learning algorithms with first-principles calculations can improve melting-temperature prediction accuracy for high-entropy alloys.
Integrating machine-learning algorithms with first-principles calculations can reduce the computational cost of melting-property predictions for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach is applicable across a wide range of high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The proposed approach is applicable across a wide range of high-entropy-alloy structures.
Electronic structure and thermodynamic properties mediate the effect of the integrated approach on melting-property predictions.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns in the electronic structure of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns in the thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
Learning electronic-structure and thermodynamic patterns enables more accurate melting-temperature predictions.
Learning electronic-structure and thermodynamic patterns enables more accurate prediction of other melting properties.
Current first-principles calculations constitute a baseline prediction capability for high-entropy alloys.
Empirical models constitute a current baseline for predicting high-entropy-alloy melting properties.
The proposed approach should be limited to high-entropy alloys for which experimental training and validation data are available.
Machine-learning predictions are uncertain for high-entropy alloys with limited or no experimental data.
Prediction accuracy can be compared using mean absolute error in predicted melting temperatures.
Computational efficiency can be compared using computational time required for predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the integrated approach does not significantly improve both accuracy and computational efficiency relative to current methods.
